codes.title: Conflicting quest ownership
codes.summary: Multiple definitions claim one quest identity.
codes.impact: The conflicting definition cannot be safely enrolled.
codes.action: Keep one owner for that ID; review the named mod files.
codes.causes: Two mods or duplicate files declare the same quest identity; an old and new release may both be enabled.
codes.troubleshooting: Find the named owners and declaration files in the original event. Disable only the duplicate release or ask the authors to resolve ownership; do not rename persistence IDs in an existing save.

codes.title: Registry enrollment is not ready
codes.summary: The complete mounted registry is not certified yet.
codes.impact: Automatic cleanup stays disabled; verified content can still run.
codes.action: Wait for registration, then check framework and content versions.
codes.causes: Startup enrollment is still running, a content module has not registered, or a declaration was rejected earlier.
codes.troubleshooting: Wait for startup to finish, then locate the first registry rejection before this message. Check the matching mod, framework and game versions. Do not enable pruning to force readiness.

codes.title: Client and server content differ
codes.summary: Verified registry fingerprints do not match.
codes.impact: Session policy determines the affected owner or operation; a content difference alone does not prove the whole session was rejected. This is not a latency measurement.
codes.action: Compare the named owner and protocol/build details; align required content before retrying the affected operation.
codes.causes: The compared client/server registry identities differ. This reference does not mean every content difference rejects the entire session; the original message identifies the affected operation.
codes.troubleshooting: Compare the named owner and protocol/build information on host and client. Update that content on both sides and reconnect normally; do not treat latency tuning as a registry fix.

codes.title: Wearable contract is not enrolled
codes.summary: The native wearable contract is not certified.
codes.impact: Unsupported wearable work is skipped rather than guessed.
codes.action: Check the equipment definition and native slot contract.
codes.causes: A wearable declaration is missing its supported native slot contract, or its enrollment was rejected.
codes.troubleshooting: Check the named equipment definition and earlier enrollment errors. Verify its slot and cooked class against the current game version; leave unsupported equipment unequipped.

codes.title: A runtime task took too long
codes.summary: A measured work slice exceeded its reporting threshold.
codes.impact: This attributes slow work; it does not prove network rejection or save corruption.
codes.action: Inspect the phase and elapsed time; prefer compatible caches and incremental refresh.
codes.causes: A measured game-thread work slice exceeded its threshold, often during discovery, refresh or a large content pass.
codes.troubleshooting: Compare the named phase, elapsed_ms, peak_ms and slow_calls. Use a compatible bundle and incremental refresh first. Report repeatable slow phases with game/storefront versions; do not erase the entire cache as a first step.

codes.title: Item catalogue is not ready
codes.summary: A catalogue or cursor is unavailable, changed or expired.
codes.impact: Last-good cached presentation remains usable while the query is rechecked.
codes.action: Refresh once; inspect mounted-content changes if it persists.
codes.causes: The item catalogue is not ready, or a query cursor belongs to an older content generation.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep the last-good results visible. Refresh the affected query once after source changes settle. If it repeats, include the search text, category/source filters and first catalogue error in a report.

codes.title: Placement needs loaded ground
codes.summary: Ground or collision is not confirmed at the target.
codes.impact: Placement is deferred or refused, not placed at a guessed height.
codes.action: Move closer to load the area or choose another point.
codes.causes: The destination is outside loaded collision, or the placement footprint cannot be confirmed.
codes.troubleshooting: Move closer to load the target area and retry at a visible ground point. Review slope/footprint details. Do not bypass collision validation or assume the cached map provides ground height.

codes.title: Unclassified diagnostic
codes.summary: This message has no registered exact diagnostic code.
codes.impact: Original severity and raw text remain authoritative.
codes.action: Read the original subsystem message; a suggested reference is guidance, not a diagnosed cause.
codes.causes: An older or uncoded warning/error has no exact registered diagnosis. A symptom-based suggestion may accompany it.
codes.troubleshooting: Read and copy the original event and the preceding failures. Record the subsystem and versions. A suggested code is a troubleshooting lead, not proof of that cause; preserve unfamiliar code text exactly.

codes.title: File logging is unavailable
codes.summary: RuneSchema cannot open or safely archive its log.
codes.impact: File logging is disabled; UE4SS warnings and summaries remain available.
codes.action: Check folder permissions and free space; keep the previous log.
codes.causes: The mod's log or archive directory cannot be opened, storage is full, or a previous log cannot be archived safely.
codes.troubleshooting: Check free space and write access to the active RuneSchema mod folder and logs directory. Preserve the previous log. Check the UE4SS warning for the original failure and retry on the next normal launch.

codes.title: Export destination is protected
codes.summary: An export would overwrite a live log or archive.
codes.impact: No export is written to that path.
codes.action: Choose another filename outside the active log and archive paths.
codes.causes: The selected export path resolves to a live source log or a protected RuneSchema archive.
codes.troubleshooting: Export to a new filename in a separate directory. Check aliases/junctions if the displayed path looks different. Do not delete the live log to make the export succeed.

codes.title: Native API contract changed
codes.summary: A reflected function, field or parameter layout is unsupported.
codes.impact: That operation stops; arbitrary memory offsets are not substituted.
codes.action: Record the game build, storefront and framework version and update compatible components.
codes.causes: The game/storefront build exposes a reflected function or field layout that this operation does not support.
codes.troubleshooting: Record the exact function/field, game build, Steam or Game Pass, UE4SS and RuneSchema versions. Install compatible components. Do not substitute guessed memory offsets.

codes.title: Runtime is becoming ready
codes.summary: The service is not ready in this world generation.
codes.impact: Work waits or returns unavailable, not a fabricated zero.
codes.action: Wait for the world to become ready, then retry the specific operation.
codes.causes: The world, player or service is still starting, changing worlds or becoming available.
codes.troubleshooting: Wait for the current world to become ready and retry only the affected action. If it persists after loading, capture the first readiness/contract failure. An unavailable meter is not a zero reading.

codes.title: Mounted content changed
codes.summary: Content identity changed during cache work.
codes.impact: The stale result is not committed under the new identity.
codes.action: Keep last-good results while the affected owner is rechecked.
codes.causes: A mod, mounted source list or source generation changed while cache work was in progress.
codes.troubleshooting: Let the source list settle, retain the last-good cache and retry the affected owner's work. Avoid starting repeated full sweeps while mods are still mounting.

codes.title: Cache bundle format is invalid
codes.summary: The header, version, manifest or record bounds failed validation.
codes.impact: The invalid bundle is not activated.
codes.action: Download the original bundle again or ask its publisher for a supported export.
codes.causes: The file is truncated, uses an unsupported bundle version, or contains invalid manifest fields, record identities, bounds or artwork metadata.
codes.troubleshooting: Check that the selected file is an original .rsmk-cache or supported legacy .rsmk-icons export. Download it again or ask the publisher for a current export. Renaming another archive does not convert it.

codes.title: Cache does not match installed content
codes.summary: The portable identity differs or a required source is inactive.
codes.impact: Only matching source groups are used; unrelated owners remain intact.
codes.action: Use the matching build/mod or local Build / update for the affected source.
codes.causes: The installed owner fingerprints, game build, required sources or locale do not match the bundle group.
codes.troubleshooting: Inspect the affected owner and locale. Download a matching pack or use local Build / update for that owner. Unrelated matching groups can remain in use; a cache does not install the missing mod.

codes.title: Cache integrity check failed
codes.summary: Bytes do not match their declared SHA-256 or pixel layout.
codes.impact: Unverified bytes are not accepted as valid cache data.
codes.action: Retry the original download; never bypass checksums or rename an unrelated pack.
codes.causes: Downloaded or cached bytes differ from the declared SHA-256, or the pixel extent is invalid.
codes.troubleshooting: Retry the original publication and check available disk space. If the same publication still fails, report the pack identity to its owner. Never disable checksum verification.

codes.title: Cache storage limit reached
codes.summary: The operation exceeds the configured size or record limit.
codes.impact: The operation is refused without removing unrelated owners.
codes.action: Increase the limit or use explicit old-cache cleanup.
codes.causes: The import/export exceeds configured disk usage, metadata, record or artwork limits.
codes.troubleshooting: Read which limit was exceeded. Increase an exposed cache budget if appropriate, or use explicit old-cache cleanup and a smaller owner-specific bundle. Do not remove mod sources or saves.

codes.title: Cache operation cancelled
codes.summary: A user request or changed source generation cancelled work.
codes.impact: Valid cached content remains usable; incomplete metadata is not activated.
codes.action: Retry when convenient; cancellation alone is not corruption.
codes.causes: The user cancelled work, or a source-generation change invalidated the in-flight operation.
codes.troubleshooting: No repair is needed for cancellation alone. Keep committed cache content and retry after mounted sources stabilize if the operation is still wanted.

codes.title: Bundle has partial coverage
codes.summary: Only the declared observed subset was captured.
codes.impact: Missing categories and art can still use local discovery.
codes.action: Check coverage by category; a full sweep is optional.
codes.causes: A bundle captures an observed subset, or export found no indexed presentation records/artwork yet.
codes.troubleshooting: Read the coverage report and original event. Observe or build the missing category locally, or import a compatible fuller bundle. Do not interpret missing cached entries as removed gameplay content.

codes.title: Content owner cannot be verified
codes.summary: A record claims ownership unsupported by active source evidence.
codes.impact: The record is skipped; borrowed artwork never reassigns content ownership.
codes.action: Correct the publisher manifest or exact asset declarations.
codes.causes: A record's claimed owner lacks matching active-source or exact asset evidence.
codes.troubleshooting: Inspect the owner manifest and declared asset paths. Ask the publisher to correct and re-export the bundle. Shared/borrowed artwork must not change the item's owning mod.

codes.title: Cache update could not be committed
codes.summary: A staged cache update could not be safely activated.
codes.impact: The previous committed metadata remains usable.
codes.action: Check permissions and free space, then retry; keep the last-good cache.
codes.causes: A staged cache file could not be written, flushed, renamed or activated safely.
codes.troubleshooting: Check the destination's permissions and free space and preserve the last committed metadata. Retry once those are resolved; do not manually activate a partially written staging file.

codes.title: Legacy icon pack loaded
codes.summary: This is an older pixel-only .rsmk-icons pack.
codes.impact: Verified pictures can be reused, but it supplies no item or journal records.
codes.action: Use a newer .rsmk-cache bundle when published; a sweep is optional.
codes.causes: An older pixel-only icon pack was imported instead of a metadata-bearing cache bundle.
codes.troubleshooting: Pictures may still be useful; this is not an integrity failure. Import a compatible .rsmk-cache for item identities, pathing, persistence IDs and journal records when available.

codes.title: Download is unavailable
codes.summary: A download failed or no compatible publication exists.
codes.impact: Cached content and local Build / update remain available.
codes.action: Check connectivity and the supported build list, then retry later.
codes.causes: Connectivity failed, or the publication index has no pack compatible with the active build and sources.
codes.troubleshooting: Check the original download result and supported-build list. Retry later if offline; otherwise use local Build / update. Existing caches remain available.

codes.title: Download manifest was rejected
codes.summary: Remote filename, index, size or integrity metadata is unsupported.
codes.impact: The download is not imported.
codes.action: Use a supported publisher index and keep the previous cache.
codes.causes: The remote index version, filename, nesting, size or integrity metadata is unsupported or unsafe.
codes.troubleshooting: Use the project's supported publication index. Report the rejected index/pack identity to its publisher. Keep the previous cache and do not bypass path or integrity checks.

codes.title: Journal cache is an observed subset
codes.summary: Full-game journal coverage is not certified.
codes.impact: Unseen entries are not assumed absent or unlocked.
codes.action: Import a compatible journal bundle or observe additional native entries.
codes.causes: Only journal entries observed or explicitly declared in the bundle are cached.
codes.troubleshooting: Check category coverage for World, Recipes and Knowledge. Import a compatible journal bundle or observe additional entries. Cached visibility does not grant journal unlocks.

codes.title: Journal cache could not be read
codes.summary: The journal record format or text bounds failed validation.
codes.impact: The invalid record set is not used.
codes.action: Import a supported bundle or refresh the native journal cache.
codes.causes: A journal cache contains unsupported records or invalid text/page bounds.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep the original save intact. Import a supported bundle or refresh the native journal cache, then inspect the original record error if it recurs.

codes.title: Original save is protected
codes.summary: The operation targets a protected original or active save.
codes.impact: No unreviewed original-save change is performed.
codes.action: Use the copy-only editor and review its export, or close the relevant world normally.
codes.causes: The operation targets a protected original save or a character/world that is still active.
codes.troubleshooting: Use an editable copy, close the relevant world normally when required, and review the export diff. Export to a new path; never force an active-save overwrite.

codes.title: Persistence cleanup is not certified
codes.summary: Complete stable registry evidence is unavailable.
codes.impact: Uncertified sections stay unchanged. Other independently certified sections may still be cleaned; native loading continues.
codes.action: Resolve readiness first; a missing lookup is not proof of removed content.
codes.causes: The applicable stable registry evidence is unavailable for one or more sections; incomplete loading must not be mistaken for removed content.
codes.troubleshooting: Review the SECTION-SKIPPED entries. Certified sections continue independently; unresolved sections are retained. Native loading still runs, using relaxed mode and rejection fallback where enabled.

codes.title: Auto-equip is unsupported or ambiguous
codes.summary: An instance, slot or native contract cannot be confirmed.
codes.impact: Delivery and equip status stay separate; no duplicate grant is made.
codes.action: Equip manually or inspect the named instance and slot.
codes.causes: The exact delivered item instance, supported equipment slot or native equip contract is ambiguous.
codes.troubleshooting: Check delivery results separately, then equip the existing item manually if needed. Do not deliver it again merely because automatic equipping was unavailable.

codes.title: Equip result is not confirmed
codes.summary: Exact-instance readback does not prove the expected result.
codes.impact: A native acceptance flag alone is not reported as successful equipping.
codes.action: Check inventory and loadout before retrying.
codes.causes: The native call returned but exact-instance equipment readback did not confirm the intended slot/item.
codes.troubleshooting: Inspect inventory and loadout before retrying. Record the item and slot. A native acceptance flag is not proof of equipping and should not trigger another grant.

codes.title: Player reading is unavailable
codes.summary: A reading is missing, stale or unsupported.
codes.impact: It is not displayed as zero or claimed to be authoritative.
codes.action: Wait for fresh data and check support for that field.
codes.causes: A player meter, skill or equipment reading is stale, missing, out of scope or unsupported by the native contract.
codes.troubleshooting: Wait for fresh host/server data and reselect the player. Check which field is unavailable. Do not interpret missing data as dead, empty or zero.

codes.title: Host authority is required
codes.summary: The caller is not authorized for the action.
codes.impact: The action is refused; a host badge grants no privilege by itself.
codes.action: Use the authorized host/server flow and current selected character.
codes.causes: The requester lacks current host/server authority for the selected action.
codes.troubleshooting: Use the authorized host/server workflow. Confirm the selected player and permission settings; a visual host badge does not itself confer authority.

codes.title: Player or world identity changed
codes.summary: The selected character, serial or world generation is stale.
codes.impact: The action is not redirected to a different player or reused object.
codes.action: Refresh and select the current player or chest again.
codes.causes: The selected player/chest serial or world generation no longer identifies the original target.
codes.troubleshooting: Refresh and explicitly reselect the current target after reconnecting or changing worlds. Do not replay a stale action against a player with the same display name.

codes.title: Map target is not loaded
codes.summary: The selected ground, node or storage actor is unavailable.
codes.impact: Unavailable contents are not an empty chest or harvested node.
codes.action: Move closer and refresh that target.
codes.causes: The map reference exists but its live ground, resource node or storage actor is not currently loaded.
codes.troubleshooting: Move within live observation range and refresh the target. A marker is a location reference, not proof of available resources or empty chest contents.

codes.title: Resource respawn time is unverified
codes.summary: The observation does not establish an exact countdown.
codes.impact: A cached map marker never invents a timer.
codes.action: Observe a nearby live node; cached references only establish locations.
codes.causes: The live observation does not establish a native respawn deadline for this resource.
codes.troubleshooting: Observe the nearby node after harvesting and wait for fresh supported timer data. Keep the timer marked unknown until verified; do not start an invented countdown from a cached marker.

codes.title: Chest access contract is unverified
codes.summary: Lock ownership, deposit permissions or persistence semantics are unverified.
codes.impact: Direct deposits and unlock overrides stay disabled.
codes.action: Use the game interaction until its current native access path is verified.
codes.causes: The native lock, owner, deposit permission or persistence contract is not verified for this storage type.
codes.troubleshooting: Use normal game interaction. Keep direct deposits and unlock overrides disabled until this build's access contract is supported; do not infer permission from map visibility.

codes.title: Storage inventory is ambiguous
codes.summary: The building has no unique owned native inventory.
codes.impact: Contents are unavailable, not read from an unrelated component.
codes.action: Refresh the target and inspect its native component contract.
codes.causes: The selected building has no unique owned native inventory, or multiple components could be mistaken for it.
codes.troubleshooting: Refresh and inspect the selected building's component contract. Keep contents unavailable rather than selecting an unrelated inventory. Do not deposit until the inventory is uniquely identified.

codes.title: Some items were not delivered
codes.summary: One or more items failed independent delivery validation.
codes.impact: Successful deliveries are not repeated to compensate.
codes.action: Review cart results and retry only failed items after resolving their cause.
codes.causes: Individual cart entries failed native validation or delivery while other entries may have succeeded.
codes.troubleshooting: Read each placard's result and resolve only failed entries. Verify the intended recipient and availability. Never resend the entire cart to compensate for a partial failure.

codes.title: Content source is not mounted
codes.summary: A required content source is absent or unregistered.
codes.impact: Its cache cannot create gameplay definitions or prove availability.
codes.action: Mount matching content or keep its references marked unavailable.
codes.causes: The source mod is absent, disabled, unmounted or has not completed registration.
codes.troubleshooting: Enable/install the matching content and let registration finish, or leave its references unavailable. Downloading its pictures/cache alone cannot create its gameplay definitions.

codes.title: Item power-level row name is invalid
codes.summary: The game cannot interpret the power-level digits in an item's data-table row name.
codes.impact: The native power-level update for that item failed; a mapping refresh does not rename cooked rows.
codes.action: Report the named item and its row name to the content author. Correct the native row naming scheme and recook the asset.
codes.causes: ChangePowerLevelInRowName rejected a row whose expected numeric positions contain non-digits. This often indicates authored or cloned row naming, not an obsolete USMAP.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep the exact item and row name. Compare it with a working native item of the same type and power-level family. Repair the authoring definition and recook; do not delete unrelated save content or suppress the error.

codes.title: Cooked animation skeleton GUID is stale
codes.summary: A cooked animation refers to an older skeleton identity.
codes.impact: The engine reports an asset consistency warning; this alone is not proof of a corrupt save.
codes.action: The author should resave the affected source animation against its current skeleton and recook it.
codes.causes: The engine found an animation/skeleton identity mismatch left in cooked content. Registry enrollment does not repair that cooked relationship.
codes.troubleshooting: Check the exact montage or sequence in the message. Resave it in the matching Unreal project against the intended skeleton, recook and verify that the warning disappears on the target platform.

codes.title: Native package or object was not found
codes.summary: An engine package or object lookup did not resolve at the reported path.
codes.impact: A required asset may be missing, or an optional conventional-path probe may have found no asset. Read the surrounding declaration result.
codes.action: Check the exact cooked package path and mount. Do not mark a mod broken solely because an optional guessed registry path is absent.
codes.causes: A package may be unmounted, incorrectly named or unavailable; alternatively an optional conventional registry lookup may legitimately be absent while another declaration works.
codes.troubleshooting: Read the owning registrar's accepted/rejected result and exact path. Verify archive contents and mounts before changing declarations. Do not invent a native asset or treat cache artwork as package registration.

codes.title: Material shader data is invalid
codes.summary: The engine could not use a material's cooked shader map.
codes.impact: The affected material may render incorrectly; the warning is not a persistence-ID diagnosis.
codes.action: Check the named material, target platform and cooking settings. Use a matching cooked build; preserve the original error.
codes.causes: The named material lacks a usable shader map for this game/platform/cook, or the engine reports an unnamed invalid material resource.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep surrounding asset-loading errors and game/storefront versions. Compare the package with the correct cooked target. A USMAP rebuild cannot manufacture missing shader data.

codes.title: Blueprint accessed a missing object
codes.summary: A native Blueprint message reports an Accessed None object reference.
codes.impact: The reported Blueprint operation may not have completed. This reference does not identify who caused the missing object.
codes.action: Capture the Blueprint/function and first preceding error. The content author should validate that object before using it.
codes.causes: A Blueprint attempted to access an object that is absent, destroyed or not initialized at the point of use.
codes.troubleshooting: Retain the native Blueprint, function and call-site text. Inspect initialization order and earlier load failures. A suggested reference is guidance, not proof of mod ownership or a completed action.

codes.title: Native game warning or error
codes.summary: A native game warning or error has no more specific RuneSchema reference yet.
codes.impact: The original message and severity remain authoritative. This reference is not a diagnosis or a game-issued error code.
codes.action: Keep the original category, message, provider code and surrounding events. Report the first failure and when it occurred.
codes.causes: No specific classifier matched this native category and message. The original error may include an engine, EOS, HTTP or platform-owned code.
codes.troubleshooting: Read the original message and first preceding failure. Keep provider codes unchanged. Record game build, storefront and whether the event occurred during startup, play or shutdown; this generic reference does not claim a root cause.

codes.title: Vitals UI callback cleanup failed
codes.summary: The native vitals widget could not remove a registered callback.
codes.impact: The widget may be tearing down. This message alone does not establish save corruption or mod failure.
codes.action: Check whether this occurs only during exit or also during play. Preserve the callback name and earlier UI errors.
codes.causes: A native vitals-widget callback could not be removed. This can occur while widgets or their owners are being destroyed.
codes.troubleshooting: Record the exact callback and whether the UI malfunctions while playing. Compare the timestamp with world exit and shutdown. Do not mark a mod unhealthy solely because of an unattributed teardown warning.

codes.title: Native user settings unavailable
codes.summary: The game could not find its expected native user settings object.
codes.impact: Settings access may fail. During shutdown the object may already be unavailable; this is not evidence of a corrupt character save.
codes.action: Check the timing and whether settings still work while playing. Capture preceding initialization errors; do not delete saves to silence this warning.
codes.causes: A native settings access occurred before initialization, after teardown, or while its expected settings object was unavailable.
codes.troubleshooting: Check whether settings work during normal play. Preserve the earliest settings initialization failure. A shutdown-only message does not justify deleting configuration or character/world saves.

codes.title: Native crowd navigation unavailable
codes.summary: The native crowd manager could not find a RecastNavMesh instance.
codes.impact: Crowd navigation may be unavailable in the current world lifecycle stage. A teardown-only warning does not prove broken map content.
codes.action: Record the world and whether AI is affected during play. Compare with world initialization or teardown events.
codes.causes: The crowd manager did not find a RecastNavMesh in its current world. The world may be loading or already tearing down.
codes.troubleshooting: Record the world and any AI navigation symptoms during play. Keep surrounding load/teardown events. Do not generate replacement navigation data or blame a mod without asset evidence.

codes.title: Native tagged-object cleanup mismatch
codes.summary: The native registry-tag subsystem could not unregister a tagged object as expected.
codes.impact: This concerns native gameplay-object tags, not RuneSchema persistence-ID declarations. It does not authorize save pruning.
codes.action: Preserve the exact object and lifecycle stage. Investigate repeated failures during play separately from shutdown-only messages.
codes.causes: Native tagged-object registration and cleanup did not agree about an object's lifecycle.
codes.troubleshooting: Capture the full object path and preceding lifecycle messages. This is not the RuneSchema persistence-ID registry, and neither automatic pruning nor invented declarations will repair it.

codes.title: Configuration could not be loaded
codes.summary: Configuration loading failed; session defaults are being used.
codes.impact: Existing configuration files are retained. The session may not use the requested settings.
codes.action: Read the original exception and named configuration path. Correct the file or access problem before restarting.
codes.causes: Reading, validating or initializing the runtime configuration failed. The original exception distinguishes syntax, type and access failures.
codes.troubleshooting: Inspect the named settings file and original exception. The runtime is using session defaults; preserve the original instead of deleting unrelated caches or saves.

codes.title: Configuration saved with original backup
codes.summary: An explicit save replaced preserved configuration with current settings after backing up the original.
codes.impact: The original file is retained at the reported backup path; startup settings require restart.
codes.action: Review the saved settings and retain the backup if an original value needs to be recovered.
codes.causes: Current settings were explicitly saved after configuration recovery, and an original-file backup was created.
codes.troubleshooting: Review the reported backup path and resulting settings. Restart to apply startup-only preferences; restore individual original values only after checking their validity.

codes.title: Configuration save failed
codes.summary: The settings save was not completed.
codes.impact: Changes remain session-only. Any backup path in the original message should be retained.
codes.action: Check the exact write/validation error and path; do not assume preferences persisted.
codes.causes: Settings serialization, validation, backup or writing reported a failure.
codes.troubleshooting: Read the exact exception and any backup path. Check permissions and free space, then reload before retrying; session values are not proof of a successful disk save.

codes.title: Plugin catalogue discovery failed
codes.summary: Plugin catalogue discovery threw an exception before loading could proceed.
codes.impact: This plugin load pass stops; RuneSchema core continues.
codes.action: Inspect the original discovery exception, plugin manifests and directory access.
codes.causes: The plugin discovery pass threw an exception. This is different from one plugin failing its native initialization.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep the original exception and inspect plugin manifests and directory access. RuneSchema core continues; do not infer a game crash from this report.

codes.title: Declared plugin DLL is missing
codes.summary: A plugin declares a native entry point that is not a regular file at the resolved path.
codes.impact: The native plugin is skipped; its PAK content remains independently available.
codes.action: Check the named plugin's entry point and installation layout; restore the matching DLL.
codes.causes: The manifest's resolved native entry point is absent or is not a regular file.
codes.troubleshooting: Compare plugin.json with the installed DLL path. Restore the correct package without changing unrelated PAKs or UE4SS host files.

codes.title: Windows could not load a plugin DLL
codes.summary: LoadLibraryExW returned failure for the named native plugin.
codes.impact: The native plugin is skipped; other plugins continue.
codes.action: Keep the reported Windows error number and DLL path. Check architecture, dependencies and access before replacing files.
codes.causes: Windows rejected LoadLibraryExW. The retained Windows number may indicate missing dependencies, invalid architecture or access restrictions; the RS code does not select one cause.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep the exact Windows number, plugin ID and DLL path. Verify a matching x64 plugin build and its dependencies before reinstalling. Do not disable security software as a generic fix.

codes.title: Plugin API exports are missing
codes.summary: A loaded DLL lacks a mandatory Query, Initialize or Shutdown export.
codes.impact: The native plugin is unloaded before initialization.
codes.action: Install a RuneSchema plugin build with the required exports, not an arbitrary UE4SS DLL.
codes.causes: The DLL loaded but did not export all mandatory RuneSchema plugin API functions.
codes.troubleshooting: Check for RuneSchemaPlugin_Query, RuneSchemaPlugin_Initialize and RuneSchemaPlugin_Shutdown in the intended plugin build. A generic UE4SS main.dll is not interchangeable.

codes.title: Plugin identity or API contract rejected
codes.summary: The queried native descriptor does not satisfy the host's identity/API contract.
codes.impact: The incompatible native plugin is isolated; core, other plugins and PAK mounting continue.
codes.action: Align the manifest ID and DLL descriptor/API build. A version label alone does not repair the descriptor.
codes.causes: The queried descriptor was absent, too small, had a different API version/ID or lacked required identity fields.
codes.troubleshooting: Align the manifest and DLL descriptor with the running host. A manifest version mismatch alone is not this rejection; preserve the actual descriptor evidence.

codes.title: Plugin initialization contract failed
codes.summary: Initialization failed or the plugin did not register its declared capabilities.
codes.impact: Its registered services/capabilities are removed and the DLL is unloaded.
codes.action: Read earlier plugin errors and the native result; verify that all declared capabilities are registered.
codes.causes: Initialize returned failure, threw, or did not register all capabilities declared by the manifest.
codes.troubleshooting: Check preceding plugin errors and the result value. A successful return value can still fail capability verification; compare declared and registered capabilities.

codes.title: Plugin UI initialization failed
codes.summary: A plugin UI callback rejected initialization or threw an exception.
codes.impact: That UI phase did not complete; the message does not establish that all plugin services stopped.
codes.action: Keep the named plugin and rejection/exception message. Check matching frontend/core builds and earlier UI errors.
codes.causes: The UI initialization callback returned failure or threw. This does not imply every plugin service has been unloaded.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep the plugin name and callback outcome. Inspect earlier frontend/device/configuration errors and use a matching plugin build.

codes.title: Plugin Unreal initialization failed
codes.summary: A plugin Unreal initialization callback returned failure or threw an exception.
codes.impact: The plugin did not confirm Unreal initialization; core and other plugin phases continue.
codes.action: Inspect the named plugin's preceding error and reported result, rather than treating this phase failure as a complete diagnosis.
codes.causes: The Unreal initialization callback did not confirm success. An earlier plugin-specific error may explain why.
codes.troubleshooting: Read the earlier plugin messages and returned result. Do not treat this wrapper failure as a missing-asset or migration diagnosis without that evidence.

codes.title: World cleanup buffer changed during validation
codes.summary: The native world buffer no longer matched the validated cleanup input.
codes.impact: Cleanup skips the buffer; the world is unchanged by this attempt.
codes.action: Keep the original world and backup. Check lifecycle/overlapping work before retrying; do not force stale bytes into the save.
codes.causes: The native buffer pointer/length/content no longer matched the prevalidated cleanup input at commit time.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep the original save and backup. Investigate overlapping native loading or lifecycle changes. Never bypass the comparison to force a stale cleanup result.

codes.title: World cleanup contract is not safe
codes.summary: Missing building IDs were observed but the native load contract was not safe to repair.
codes.impact: The cleanup attempt leaves the world unchanged.
codes.action: Check the preceding contract and registry evidence. Missing IDs alone do not authorize writing an unverified save format.
codes.causes: Orphan IDs were detected but the verified native world-load repair contract was not satisfied.
codes.troubleshooting: Review the preceding contract/binding and registry evidence for this exact game build. Do not disable save validation merely to silence this warning.

codes.title: World cleanup repair did not complete
codes.summary: The native world-buffer repair attempt reported an exception.
codes.impact: The cleanup attempt reports the world unchanged; the original exception remains authoritative.
codes.action: Retain the original world, backups and full error. Resolve the reported validation/repair cause before retrying.
codes.causes: A world-buffer repair stage reported an exception before its cleanup could be accepted.
codes.troubleshooting: Keep the original exception and backup path. Resolve the named validation or repair condition; this code does not claim the native game save is corrupt.

codes.title: World cleanup input could not be validated
codes.summary: World data parsing or validation failed before a cleanup result could be accepted.
codes.impact: This cleanup path does not write a guessed repair.
codes.action: Keep the exact parser/validation exception and game build. A cleanup rejection alone does not prove the native game cannot load the world.
codes.causes: Native world data could not be parsed or validated by this cleanup adapter.
codes.troubleshooting: Preserve the original data and exact exception. Compare the adapter with the game build; native loading can still proceed without an invented repair.

codes.title: Game Pass world cleanup hooks unavailable
codes.summary: Required Game Pass world-loading hooks could not be installed.
codes.impact: That world cleanup path stays unavailable and does not change saves.
codes.action: Check the current Game Pass executable/build and matching RuneSchema bindings; preserve existing saves and use supported native loading.
codes.causes: One or more required Game Pass world-loading hooks were unavailable for the current executable.
codes.troubleshooting: Use a matching RuneSchema build/binding and keep the original save. Do not install a different UE4SS host just to suppress this framework cleanup warning.

bridgeReasons.title: Accepted at this stage
bridgeReasons.causes: The envelope or validation step passed, not necessarily the whole gameplay action.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Follow the same correlationId through terminal outcome and readback before claiming delivery or execution.

bridgeReasons.title: Already on native authority
bridgeReasons.causes: The observed action is already executing on the authoritative side and needs no client forwarding.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Normally no action is required. Do not forward it again.

bridgeReasons.title: Bridge not ready
bridgeReasons.causes: The player bridge is unavailable, not attached or still waiting to replicate; retries may remain pending or expire.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Wait for world/player readiness. If it persists, check cooked bridge availability and the first attachment error on host and client.

bridgeReasons.title: Duplicate observation suppressed
bridgeReasons.causes: The same local action already has a pending request.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Normally no action is required; suppression prevents duplicate execution. Inspect the original correlation rather than submitting another action.

bridgeReasons.title: Native inventory removal observed
bridgeReasons.causes: The server observed the exact consumed-item removal needed to create a short-lived authority permit.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Follow permit matching and callback completion; this intermediate observation is not proof of the final gameplay effect.

bridgeReasons.title: Execution reported at this stage
bridgeReasons.causes: The callback, activation or receipt reports execution.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Use the original stage and any final native readback. A receipt is not interchangeable with verification of every downstream effect.

bridgeReasons.title: Callback failed
bridgeReasons.causes: An authority callback threw or a request handler sent its failure receipt.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Read the first associated exception and correlationId. Check the registered graph, data and native layout before retrying; do not repeat a potentially consumed item blindly.

bridgeReasons.title: Consumption not confirmed
bridgeReasons.causes: The authority has no matching unexpired native inventory-removal permit, or its wait expired.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Check the consumable instance and native consumption path on the host. Do not invoke the effect directly or grant a duplicate item as a workaround.

bridgeReasons.title: Player no longer available
bridgeReasons.causes: A pending request lost its original player object.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Reconnect and explicitly select the current character. Old requests must not be redirected to a new player object.

bridgeReasons.title: Unclassified bridge failure
bridgeReasons.causes: An exception did not match the bridge's coarse diagnostic classification.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Capture the original exception, channel, stage and correlationId. This fallback alone does not identify a specific root cause.

bridgeReasons.title: Legacy transport used
bridgeReasons.causes: The request was transmitted using the supported legacy route.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: This is not automatically an error. Follow its receipt and keep client/server framework versions compatible.

bridgeReasons.title: Request rate exceeded
bridgeReasons.causes: The bridge's request budget for this requester was exceeded.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Stop repeated clicks or automated resubmission and retry at a normal rate. Mod authors should deduplicate requests rather than disable the limit.

bridgeReasons.title: Stale request revision
bridgeReasons.causes: The incoming revision is not newer than the requester's last accepted revision.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Refresh the current state and send a genuinely new request only if still needed. Never replay old envelopes.

bridgeReasons.title: Authority work deferred
bridgeReasons.causes: A request was accepted but awaits its required authority-side condition.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Follow the same correlation to completion or expiry. Accepted/deferred is not completed; do not trigger a second grant.

bridgeReasons.title: Compatibility handshake rejected
bridgeReasons.causes: The compatibility receipt was unsuccessful. The current session handler rejects a different protocol; other differences can be reported permissively.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Read the original handshake detail and compare protocol/framework versions. Do not assume every registry or mapping difference rejects the session.

bridgeReasons.title: Registry action missing
bridgeReasons.causes: The bridge classified an exception containing 'not registered'. The required action key may not have enrolled.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Inspect the original exception and owning declaration. Resolve enrollment before retrying; this classification is guidance, not an independent registry check.

bridgeReasons.title: Callback contract mismatch
bridgeReasons.causes: The bridge classified an exception mentioning a layout or contract mismatch.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Inspect the exact reflected function/parameters and supported game build. Use compatible components, never guessed offsets.

bridgeReasons.title: Request expired
bridgeReasons.causes: A diagnostic result reports expiry after its allowed wait.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Inspect its stage and original detail to identify the missing prerequisite. Refresh current state before making a new request.

bridgeReasons.title: World changed
bridgeReasons.causes: Pending work was cancelled at the old world's boundary.
bridgeReasons.troubleshooting: Normally no repair is required. Wait for the new world and explicitly select current targets before starting new actions.
